summary: Read-only frontend consultation on brief r1 at baseline 64ea43cd (clean tree). I read the spec, the prototype logic, the dashboard AGENTS.md, .memory rules and every file in scope, plus the server handlers and orchestrator paths they call. I did not run any tests or builds.

Q1: yes. One App-level 'now' that ticks every second, only while statusAvailable && run alive && some stage has an open interval, should feed one pure per-render computation. Both StagesList and CostPanel then get the same numbers by construction. App already re-renders every second (useElapsed) and nothing in the tree is memoized, so the extra render cost is negligible.

The draft is sound overall but needs these changes. (1) Removing the kebab also removes the only Attach-helper entry point in collaboration_mode=assistants and when collaboration is on without the mesh, so the user must decide. (2) One rounding rule so that Working+Waiting+Paused, the Waiting reasons and Stage total add up in the seconds shown. (3) setStageNote cannot tell 409 (saved, may miss the first prompt) from 400 (not saved) with today's postJson; move it to jsonRequest/FlowApiError. (4) Header buttons must not be feed-only, must be disabled during a review pause and must show their errors outside showControls. (5) agent-note-modal.css holds modal styles shared by 9 dialogs, and the skin source is skins/base, not public/skins. (6) Explicit decisions are needed on '45s' vs the prototype's '0m 45s', the footer label (Stage total vs run-wide money), Enter vs Cmd+Enter, and no 'Included at start' label.
Findings f14 and f15 give the exact removal list and a minimal Vitest plan.

findings.detail: Removing the kebab drops the only Attach-helper entry point in two supported configurations. After removal the only entry is StagePeoplePanel (App.tsx:817-836, onAttachHelper at :825). It renders only when showPeople = stageMesh && collaborationMode === 'team' && view === 'feed' (App.tsx:421, :462). In collaboration_mode: assistants, or with capabilities.collaboration on but the mesh probe off, the kebab item (StagesList.tsx:519-531) is the only way to open AttachHelperDialog. App.test.tsx:3041 ('assistants mode: the stage menu still offers Attach helper…') explicitly guards this. The spec says both 'use the existing People button, add no new buttons' and 'check availability under current capability gates and collaboration modes'; here those conflict. Recommendation: ask the user before implementing, with two options. (a) Accept the loss in assistants/no-mesh mode, turn that test into a negative test and document it in docs/dashboard.md. (b) Authorize reusing the existing People-style 'Attach helper' control in the WorkspaceHeader actions slot when !showPeople && canAttachHelper(stage, collaboration). Do not silently delete the test.

The numbers shown won't add up unless rounding happens once. If the rail and Cost each format raw ms with floor(ms/1000), then Working 1.6 s + Waiting 1.6 s displays as 1s + 1s next to Time 3s. The Waiting reasons can stop summing to Waiting, and Stage total (a sum of raw ms) can differ from the sum of the row times shown. The spec requires Time = Working + Waiting + Paused, reasons summing to Waiting, and UI tests of sums across parallel stages. Recommendation: the pure helper returns whole seconds. First add the live delta to the open kind's leaf (work, approval, helpers, backoff, scheduling or paused), then floor each leaf. Then derive waiting = sum of reasons, total = work + waiting + paused, Stage total = sum of row totals, and Stage work/waiting/paused = sums of the leaves. The rail, the Cost rows, the expanded breakdown and the summary all read these same derived integers.

setStageNote uses postJson, which throws a plain Error('POST … -> 409') with no status field (run-client.ts:7-17, :87-89). The editor must tell apart three cases: 400 'stage is X, not pending' (pkg/server/handlers.go:296-299, nothing saved); 409 (handlers.go:312-316, file saved but may miss the first prompt); and anything else (retryable). Recommendation: switch setStageNote to the existing jsonRequest('POST') path. It throws FlowApiError with .status (run-client.ts:19-31, :52-65), and plain-text error bodies fall back to FlowApiError(url, status). The caller checks err instanceof FlowApiError && err.status. No new error primitive and no endpoint change: the memory rule 'remove only the trigger' keeps /api/stages/<id>/note and /button untouched.

Don't delete the file. Besides the kebab rules it holds styles other components use. .modal-overlay/.modal-content are used by AttachHelperDialog, AttachAssistantDialog, AddStageDialog, ReviewNotesModal, FileBrowserModal, BoardView, AddRunAgentDialog, BoardTaskDetails and FileCommentSendDialog. .modal-actions is shared too. .modal-attention-row/.modal-attention-shortcut and @keyframes modalAttnPulse are used by ReviewNotesModal. All four skins @import the file (skins/{coffee,goga,graphite,novacorps}/index.css). Delete only .stage-kebab-wrap, .stage-kebab*, .stage-kebab-menu* and .stage-kebab-divider, plus .agent-note-warning/.agent-note-textarea unless StageNote reuses them, and fix the header comment. Renaming the file would touch four skin imports and isn't needed.

Spec §6 says to edit public/skins/base/, but the source is pkg/web/dashboard/skins/base/. sync-skins.js:6-7 runs rmSync on public/skins and copies skins/ over it on every npm dev/build. public/skins is tracked, so edit skins/base, run sync (the build does it) and commit both; edits made only in public/skins are wiped by the next build. If the new time cells or .stage-time use the mono font, add their selectors to MONO_ALLOWED in src/skins/skins-contract.test.ts (~:620-630); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums alone needs no contract change.

Placement: a sibling between .status-badge-wrap (:54-72) and attentionNav/.workspace-header-actions (:73-98), e.g. <span className='workspace-stage-buttons' role='group' aria-label='Stage buttons'>. Draw the separator as the group's border-inline-start (prototype refinements.css:496), so no separate separator node needs hiding. Visibility: a new prop from App (selection?.kind === 'stage') && !stage.isScript && status ∈ {running, awaiting_approval} && stage.buttons.length > 0. Do not reuse showControls (view==='feed' && stage selection, App.tsx:732). The kebab offered buttons from every view, and selecting an awaiting_approval stage auto-opens the Approval attention view (App.tsx:352-355), where WorkspaceHeader is still rendered (App.tsx:727). Feed-only gating would hide these buttons exactly when awaiting_approval is shown. The prototype has only a feed heading, so this doesn't break parity. Errors: .workspace-action-error is gated by showControls (:99). Render it when showControls || buttonsShown, otherwise a button failure in the Approval view is invisible.

Disable the buttons when (a) !statusAvailable; (b) flowPauseState !== 'none' — Orchestrator.Button calls rejectIfReviewPaused first (:235-237), so every button fails during a review pause; (c) a Pause-on-focus operation is active. App's controlsEnabled (App.tsx:733) already encodes (b) and (c), and for running/awaiting_approval it reduces to exactly that, so reuse it. In-flight: send through the shared useStageAction(stage).send(id => triggerStageButton(id, label)) (hooks/use-stage-retry/use-stage-retry.ts:24-57). It locks per status@updatedAt episode across navigation, shares the lock with Pause/Retry so Pause can't race a just-sent button, and stores the error the header already renders. Button → Revise moves the stage to revising, so the lock clears on the next poll or WS-triggered refresh. ErrNotApplied returns 409 and shows as a retryable error. Delete App.handleButton and its stale comment (App.tsx:128-133). Narrow widths: at ≤600 px (layout.css:782-788), give the group an order after the actions and flex-basis: 100% so it wraps under title/status. Elsewhere use min-width: 0; overflow-x: auto; flex: 0 1 auto so it shrinks/scrolls rather than pushing People/Pause (.workspace-header-actions is margin-left: auto; flex-shrink: 0, layout.css:336-342). Leave padding so focus outlines aren't clipped by the overflow.

The prototype's formatTime (tmp/redesign-sandbox/app.js:361-367) renders 45 s as '0m 45s' and pads seconds ('3m 05s'). The brief's draft says '45s', and spec §3.5 only fixes '0s' and the '3m 12s' / '1h 02m 03s' shapes. Record an explicit decision. Recommendation: '45s' under a minute as an approved deviation, and keep zero padding ('3m 05s', '1h 02m 03s') for tabular alignment. Don't reuse RunMetrics' private formatDuration (MM:SS, :192-199); put the new formatter in a pure lib module. Format Cost's 'Run elapsed' from the same elapsedMs App already computes (App.tsx:465), so header and Cost show the same value. Display states: no timing (old server) or started=false → '—'; started with 0 ms → '0s'; complete=false → '—' with an explanatory title, not a partial number presented as a measurement.

For a started stage the prototype labels the note 'Included at start' (app.js:162); spec §5.4 forbids claiming that from file presence alone. Use neutral copy instead ('Saved before start' / 'Read only'). Show a delivery warning only for a 409 observed in this page session. Keep that outcome in the run+stage draft entry so it survives tab/stage switches; after a reload the neutral label is shown. Suggested 409 copy: 'Saved, but the stage started at the same moment — the agent may not have received this note. Use the Feed composer to send it now.' Suggested 400 copy: 'Not saved — the stage has already started.' Keep the draft in both cases.

Today the footer row is 'Total' with run-wide tokens/money including overhead. The prototype footer reads 'Stage total' and sums stage tokens/cost (app.js renderCost). That contradicts spec §4.3: the money Total stays run-wide including Run overhead, and the time total is labelled Stage total. Recommendation: keep the row label 'Total'; the Time cell shows Stage total with a visible sub-label 'Stage total'. Add a note under the table: 'Stage total sums stage times and can exceed Run elapsed; token and cost totals are run-wide, including Run overhead.' In time-only mode, label the row 'Stage total' and omit the Run overhead row, which has neither time nor usage.

Q1 answer: yes, structured as follows. useStageClock(active): number returns a 'now' that updates every second only while active = statusAvailable && runAlive (App.tsx:451) && stages.some(s => s.timing?.open != null). When inactive it keeps the last value (the stale freeze). When active flips back it reads Date.now() immediately, so after an outage the value jumps forward, never backwards. A pure stageTimes(stages, now, live) → ReadonlyMap<stageId, StageTimeView | null> is computed in App on each render and passed to both StagesList and CostPanel; the Cost summary sums come from the same map. If the two components ran their own hooks/intervals they'd read different Date.now() values and could differ by a second at boundaries. Live delta = max(0, now − Date.parse(open.since)), added only while live. Ignore open defensively when runStatus is finished/failed/interrupted. Re-render cost: App already re-renders every second during a live run (useElapsed sets state on each tick) and only AssistantActivityRow is memoized, so the rail and Cost already re-render every second. A second interval adds at most one more App render per second, and with nothing open there's no interval at all. Shared limitation with useElapsed: client/server clock skew shifts the live delta, but rail==Cost is unaffected.

Q2 edits. In App: delete the accounting guard effect (App.tsx:320-323) and push the Cost tab unconditionally (App.tsx:568-571). The reducer needs no change ('openCost' at workspace-view.ts:216 has no accounting gate); handleOpenCost/costFocusPending stay. In CostPanel, replace the two whole-panel early returns (:60-75) with two flags. usage = accounting.supported && accounting.hasData shows the Tokens column, Run overhead row, run-wide Total, UsageBreakdown, CoverageBadge and TokenMixBar/FigureGrid in expansions. money = usage && accounting.showMoney shows the Est. cost column. Time column and summary always render. When accounting is supported but !hasData, show the old messages inline under the time table ('No usage data', or 'Cost unavailable this run' when health=unavailable). Keep the unavailable banner (:131-135) when hasData. Rows: all stages in status order, not only s.cost != null (:77-79). A row is expandable when it has a started timing or a cost; a pending, never-started stage shows a plain label and '—'. Column span becomes 2 + usage + money (replaces :57-58); the subtitle follows the mode. New props: the stageTimes map, elapsedMs, startedAt ('—' before start). Show the coverage badge only in usage mode — it says nothing about time completeness; mark incomplete timing separately. GlobalHeader/RunMetrics are unchanged; their cost tiles open Cost only under accounting.supported, as before.

detail: Placement. Inside FeedWorkspace's column, through a new optional slot prop (e.g. aboveFeed?: ReactNode) rendered between .feed-filter-row and #feed-content.feed-scroll (:208-215). This matches the prototype (app.js:184 puts it in .feed-main before the scroll area) and leaves the People panel column (App.tsx:817) alone. The slot must be optional because team/ActivityPanel.tsx:18 also renders FeedWorkspace. Outside the scroll container, useStickToBottom's MutationObserver doesn't see editing, and its ResizeObserver (use-stick-to-bottom.ts:69) keeps a stuck feed at the bottom when the note grows. Give the block a bounded max-height with its own overflow (smaller at 390 px).

Gating. App renders the block only when wsState.view === 'feed' && selection?.kind === 'stage' && workspaceStage !== null — the same 'stage, not helper' rule as the header buttons. When a helper is selected and the user clicks the Feed tab, the parent feed is shown without the note. Use key={stage.id}. pending && !isScript → 'Add note', or the text plus 'Edit note'. Otherwise a non-empty preNote is read-only. Otherwise no block. A manual Retry (failed → pending) makes the note editable again under the server gate (handlers.go:296-299); confirm this with the user.

Draft store. A separate App-level, run-scoped, copy-on-write Map<stageId, StageNoteDraft> in a ref, reset on runEpoch — the same pattern as composerDrafts (App.tsx:431-446), but not merged into ComposerDraft because delivery semantics differ (memory: don't merge look-alike features). An entry means the editor is open: {text, saving?, error?, outcome?: 'missed-start' | 'not-saved'}. Keystrokes go to local state and are written through to the ref without an App re-render; open, close and outcome changes trigger a re-render. Returning to the stage shows the editor marked as an unsaved draft (memory: 'Drafts and workspace continuity').

Editing behavior. Reuse PasteableTextarea with allowFileReferences, as the old modal did (AgentNoteModal.tsx:49-61); finished image uploads are already in the text, and in-flight uploads are lost on unmount (acceptable). Focus: a focused textarea is already covered by useIsEditing; an open but unfocused editor doesn't block attention, and the App store keeps the draft when the view switches. Remove preNoteModalStageId from otherModalsOpen (App.tsx:168). After Save/Cancel/Remove, move focus to the Add/Edit note button (prototype app.js:784). Call refresh() after a successful save so pre_note and the rail icon update without waiting up to 3 s. Ignore a response if the run or stage changed while it was in flight (check runEpoch and stageId).

Races. If the stage starts while editing, keep the draft, render it read-only with the reason and a 'Discard draft' action, and never auto-delete it. pre_note can also change on the server (feedback intents write prenote.md for pending stages, pkg/orchestrator/feedback_intent.go:281-284), so polling must never overwrite an open draft. Composer drafts and the helper selection aren't touched.

run-client keeps setStageNote and triggerStageButton (memory: when removing a UI entry point, remove only the trigger).
Minimal Vitest set, using fake timers the way App.test.tsx:902-916 already does (vi.useFakeTimers, vi.setSystemTime, act(advanceTimersByTimeAsync)):

(1) Pure lib/stage-timing tests. Formats: 0 → '0s'; 45 s → decided format; '3m 05s'; '1h 02m 03s'; ≥100 h. A never-started stage (no timing or started=false) → '—' vs '0s' for a started stage with a zero interval. The live delta goes only to the open kind's leaf. After rounding, Waiting = sum of reasons and Time = sum of leaves. complete=false → '—'. Ended run → open ignored.
(2) useStageClock: ticks every second while active; statusAvailable=false freezes the value and registers no interval; returning to fresh jumps to Date.now(); no open interval → no interval.

(3) One App test: a running stage with an open work interval; open Cost; advance 61 s; the rail's .stage-time text equals the Cost row's Time cell. Make /api/status fail and advance more than 6 s → both frozen. Respond with run_status finished and open=null → both fixed, unchanged after another 5 s. A pending stage shows '—' in both.

(4) CostPanel: time-only when accounting is unsupported (no Tokens/Est. cost/coverage/overhead row; Time and summary present); supported && !hasData → time table + inline 'No usage data'; unavailable && !hasData → inline 'Cost unavailable this run'; usage mode keeps the overhead row with Time '—' and the run-wide Total; show_money=false hides money; an expanded row shows the time breakdown and TokenMixBar/FigureGrid; a script stage without cost is listed. Rewrite CostPanel.test.tsx:77-96.

(5) StageNote, component level plus the App store: Add → type → switch stage/tab → return keeps the draft; Cancel restores the saved text; Save posts and closes; Remove posts ''; Cmd/Ctrl+Enter saves; Escape cancels without bubbling; 409 keeps the draft and warns without 'Included at start'; 400 shows 'not saved'; the stage going running mid-edit → read-only with the draft kept; helper selection, script stages and started-empty stages show no block; text is escaped; the composer draft is untouched.

(6) WorkspaceHeader: the group and separator are absent for a helper selection, a script stage, non-live statuses and empty buttons; YAML order is preserved; disabled when the status is stale or flowPauseState ≠ none; locked after a click until a new episode; errors visible; only the label is posted to /api/stages/<id>/button; present in the Approval view.
(7) StagesList: no 'More actions' anywhere; time on the status line; the note icon has an accessible label.

findings.detail: PasteableTextarea's onSubmit fires on plain Enter, and also on Cmd/Ctrl+Enter because metaKey isn't excluded; Shift+Enter inserts a newline. The spec asks for Cmd/Ctrl+Enter to save and Escape to cancel, and the prototype keeps plain Enter as a newline (app.js:604-606). Decide explicitly between two options. Reuse onSubmit: dashboard AGENTS.md wants one shared submit behavior, and the old pre-note modal saved on Enter. Or omit onSubmit and handle Cmd/Ctrl+Enter in onKeyDown so multi-line notes are easy to write. Either way: the Escape handler calls e.stopPropagation(), as StagesList.tsx:191-193 does, so window-level Escape listeners (Maximizable.tsx:13-16, the People drawer at StagePeoplePanel.tsx:116-121) don't fire too. Disable Save while the trimmed text is empty: Remove note is the delete path, and SavePreNote treats whitespace as a delete (pkg/state/state.go:898). Disable Save/Remove and the textarea while a request is pending.

Put .stage-time on the status line inside the row button (.stage-label holds the status word and the time, :368-371). Mark the ticking digits aria-hidden: a focused button whose accessible name changes every second can be re-announced, and the spec forbids a stream of announcements. The Cost table keeps readable numbers without aria-live. Replace the 📝 span (:392, outside the button, title only) with a small icon inside .stage-name that has role='img', aria-label='Stage note attached' and a title (prototype app.js:128). Keep the rail cost in .stage-actions under the existing railCost rules (:98-110).

suggested_change: 1) Before implementing, ask the user about Attach helper in assistants mode and collaboration without the mesh (f1).

2) Frontend timing: useStageClock(active) plus a pure stageTimes(stages, now, live) computed once in App; floor each leaf, then derive the sums (f2, f11). Single formatter in lib with an explicit decision on '45s' (f8).

3) Cost: always show the tab; remove the App guard effect; CostPanel uses usage/money flags instead of whole-panel empty states; all stages listed; Total row keeps run-wide money and labels the time sum as Stage total (f10, f12).

4) Header buttons: group after the status badge, gated by stage selection (not view), live statuses, non-script and non-empty buttons; reuse controlsEnabled and useStageAction; show errors when the group is visible; wrap below at ≤600 px (f6, f7).

5) Stage note: optional slot in FeedWorkspace between the filter row and the scroll area; App-level run-scoped copy-on-write draft map; setStageNote via jsonRequest/FlowApiError so 400 and 409 are told apart; neutral 'saved before start' copy, never 'Included at start'; decide Enter vs Cmd/Ctrl+Enter; Escape with stopPropagation (f3, f9, f13, f16).
6) Kebab removal exactly as listed in f14; keep the shared modal CSS; edit skins/base, then sync to public/skins (f4, f5); test rewrites and new tests per f14/f15.
limitations: Read-only consultation: no web tests, typecheck, lint or build were run, and no browser or visual check. I did not open the prototype screenshots (evidence/*.png); visual and layout statements come from the prototype CSS/JS and the product CSS.

The backend timing contract (field names, the open interval and complete semantics, and run-end handling) is taken from the coordinator's draft design and was not reviewed here; the frontend recommendations assume the server sends open=null after the run ends.
Line numbers are from baseline 64ea43cd. Docs (docs/dashboard.md, docs/flow-reference.md) were not reviewed.
Recommending f1 option (b) would touch the spec's 'no new buttons' constraint and is left to the user.
